profile.name: Ipca Laboratories Ltd
profile.founded: Incorporated in Mumbai on 19-Oct-1949 as The Indian Pharmaceutical Combine Association Ltd (renamed Ipca Laboratories in 1964); Premchand Godha joined the board in Oct-1975 when the Bachchan family invested, became MD in 1983; in 1997 the Bachchan family sold its 36% to the four whole-time directors (the Godha and Chandurkar families today)
profile.what: Integrated Indian drug maker: branded formulations in India (rank 16 in the IPM, 2.08% share, 22 divisions, ~172 brands, ~7,000 medical reps), branded formulations in emerging markets (Africa, CIS, Asia, LatAm), generic formulations for the UK/EU, Australia/NZ, Canada and the US, institutional anti-malarial tenders, and ~80 APIs (75% exported). Owns 52.67% of listed Unichem Laboratories (US generics, Europe, Brazil, APIs).
profile.employees: 18,667 permanent employees at Mar-26 (1,035 overseas), of whom 10,308 in marketing and distribution
profile.plants: Formulations: Pithampur SEZ Indore, Piparia (Silvassa), Athal, Ratlam, Sikkim, Dehradun and others; APIs: Ratlam (largest), Tarapur, Mahad, Dewas, new Wardha intermediates unit (commercial production Feb-2026). Under construction: Dewas formulations (₹275 cr), Pithampur monoclonal antibodies (₹250 cr), Pisgah Forest NC liquid injectables (US$22 mn). Sold in FY26: Tarapur T-139 formulations unit and Ankleshwar API unit (slump sales)
profile.rd: R&D ₹246.09 cr in FY26 (3.37% of standalone turnover; ₹207.08 cr, 3.12% in FY25); centres at Mumbai, Ratlam, Athal (Silvassa), Ranu (Vadodara). 46 ANDAs filed (32 approved), 50 US DMFs, 62 EDQM certificates of suitability; 7 biosimilar candidates (2 have completed engineering batches)

q1fy27.iqvia: Ipca +11.7% on IQVIA (chronic 17.2% vs market 15.2%; acute 8.9% vs 4.5%); rank 16, market share 2.08%; anti-malarials −24%, now ~1% of the domestic business; pain +13%, cardio-diabetic +17%, CNS +19%, derma +17%, urology +25%, ophthalmology +17%; ~5% volume, 4.5-5% price, ~2% new products
q1fy27.exportsNote: Export formulations +34% to ₹603 cr: branded +16% (₹143 cr), generics ex-tenders +27% (₹340 cr; Europe/UK ₹33 cr → ₹137 cr per management, US shipments +8%), institutional +107% (₹112 cr, incl. ~₹40 cr of March shipments delayed to April). APIs +30% to ₹424 cr (export +33%, domestic +20%)
q1fy27.unichemNote: US business +27% (Unichem's own portfolio +9%, Ipca's products sold through Unichem USA much faster), Europe +3%, Brazil +52%, ROW (Acacia) ₹8 cr → ₹17 cr, APIs ₹33-34 cr → ₹58 cr; margin 11% (+680bp YoY); FY27 guidance kept at +10% revenue and 13% EBITDA margin

fy27: Consolidated revenue growth 14-16% (raised on 14-Aug-2026 from 12-13% given on 1-Jun-2026); guidance in rupee terms
Consolidated EBITDA margin ~23% (raised from ~22%; FY26 20.7%); includes higher freight and logistics costs
Domestic formulations growth 12-13% (1-2pp from new products; price rises of 6-7% on non-controlled products to offset input costs)
Unichem: revenue +10%, EBITDA margin 12-13% (from ~8% in FY26); Ireland plant closed (saves €4-5 mn a year)
Capex ₹700-800 cr (Pithampur extended-release capacity, Dewas and Wardha API/intermediates, biotech pilot plants ~₹100 cr, continuous processing)
US: 7-8 launches a year across Ipca and Unichem; 4-5 new Ipca filings a year; Ipca US growth potential 15-17% a year
Debt: ~₹193 cr at Jun-26; ~₹70 cr term loans at Mar-27, repaid in FY28; no working-capital debt
Medium term: Ipca standalone margin ~30% (from ~26%); consolidated 25-26% in 2-3 years; biosimilar revenue from FY29-30

unichem.block: 2,35,01,440 shares (33.38%) bought from a promoter shareholder (the Mehta family) under an SPA announced 24-Apr-2023 at ₹440 a share (₹1,034 cr announced; recorded at ₹945.35 cr)
unichem.openOffer: Mandatory open offer for 26% at ₹440: 19.29% tendered (₹597.50 cr); closed 8-Sep-2023; Unichem became a subsidiary
unichem.consolidated: Associate after the block (Q1FY24), subsidiary from Q2FY24 (Sep-2023)
unichem.mergerStatus: No scheme to merge Unichem into Ipca had been announced by 30-Sep-2026. Ipca's board approved a scheme to merge Krebs Biochemicals (49.65% associate) on 26-Jun-2026 (appointed date 1-Apr-2026; 7 Ipca shares per 200 Krebs shares; promoters 44.72% → 44.66%), subject to approvals. Bayshore Pharmaceuticals (US) was sold during FY26 after its US generics business was folded into Unichem Pharmaceuticals (USA), which now sells Ipca's US products

fy26.patNote: includes the Jogeshwari land sale (₹279 cr consideration; only ₹17.65 cr gain in Ipca's books after the acquisition fair value) and EU interest ₹58.26 cr

unichem.euFine: EU perindopril (Servier) case: €13.96 mn fine (2014) provided in FY24 (₹125.62 cr); with interest €19.55 mn (₹203.89 cr) demanded 17-Sep-2025 and settled 28-Oct-2025
unichem.src: Ipca press release 24-Apr-2023; Ipca filing on completion of the open offer (Sep-2023); AR FY26 (investments note: 3,70,81,011 shares, ₹1,542.85 cr; BRSR list of subsidiaries; note 32); Medical Dialogues (28-Jun-2026) for the Krebs scheme; Screener.in (UNICHEMLAB, consolidated); NSE close 30-Sep-2026

timeline.event: Ipca voluntarily halted US shipments from the Ratlam API plant after a USFDA inspection found data-integrity lapses
USFDA import alert on the Ratlam API plant (four APIs exempted)
Import alerts on the Pithampur (SEZ Indore) and Piparia (Silvassa) formulation plants; Canada followed
Warning letter covering all three plants
Temporary exemption for chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine during COVID-19, withdrawn by Jul-2020

All three plants re-inspected (Ratlam and Pithampur in Jun-2023, with a Form 483 for Pithampur; Silvassa during the year); Establishment Inspection Reports classified them VAI (SEZ Indore EIR, Oct-2023) and the import alerts were lifted; Ipca began commercialising its own US products through Unichem's US front end
Tarapur API plant: USFDA inspection 1-5 Dec 2025 with 3 observations; classified VAI (announced 9-Feb-2026)
WHO prequalification inspections of Pithampur SEZ (Jun-2025) and Ratlam FPP/API (Sep-Oct 2025)
Unichem: Goa formulations VAI after a Jul-2024 inspection (5 observations); Roha API and Pithampur (Unichem) VAI in 2025
Unichem Kolhapur API plant: 5 procedural observations, none on data integrity; no EIR reported by 30-Sep-2026
Unichem Goa formulations plant (its main US plant): 5 observations described as procedural; response due within 15 days (filing 27-Sep-2026)

regulatory.status30Sep: No Ipca or Unichem plant was under a USFDA import alert or warning letter on 30-Sep-2026. Two Unichem inspections were open (Kolhapur API: no EIR reported; Goa formulations: 5 observations on 26-Sep-2026).

governance.promoters: Two promoter families: the Godhas (Kaygee Investments 25.49%, Kaygee Laboratories 6.61%, Premchand Godha 2.29%, others) and the Chandurkars (Chandurkar Investments 5.50%, Usha Chandurkar 1.70%, Sameer Chandurkar 0.79%); 44.72% in all (17 entities), no pledge. history.event: Incorporated in Mumbai as The Indian Pharmaceutical Combine Association Ltd (Ipca Laboratories from 1964)
Premchand Godha joins the board (Oct-1975) as the Bachchan family invests; MD from 1983; the Bachchans sell their 36% to the four whole-time directors in 1997
history.impact: Today's two promoter families (Godha, Chandurkar); pain, anti-malarials and API backward integration built over these decades

history.event: USFDA import alerts on Ratlam (Jan-2015), Pithampur and Silvassa (Mar-2015); warning letter (Feb-2016)
history.impact: US business shut; FY16 revenue −9% and EBITDA margin 10%; remediation costs for years

history.event: COVID-19 demand for hydroxychloroquine (HCQS) and other APIs
history.impact: EBITDA margin 29%, EPS ₹44.9 (a peak not seen again until FY26)

history.event: Share split: each ₹2 share into two ₹1 shares (25.37 cr shares)
Bought 40.98% of Lyka Labs (JV) and kept raising its Krebs Biochemicals exposure
history.impact: Both loss-making; ₹130 cr of Krebs impairments in FY24-25

history.event: HCQ normalisation, institutional tender collapse, API price and input-cost squeeze
Acquired 52.67% of Unichem Laboratories for ₹1,543 cr (block from the promoters plus open offer)
history.impact: Revenue +24% in FY24; margin diluted (Unichem ~5% then); debt and interest up; EU fine provision ₹126 cr

history.event: USFDA lifts the import alerts on Ratlam, Pithampur and Silvassa after VAI re-inspections
history.impact: US commercialisation through Unichem USA; consolidated US sales ₹1,567 cr in FY26

history.event: Sold Bayshore (US) after merging its business into Unichem USA; sold Tarapur formulations and Ankleshwar API units; Unichem sold Jogeshwari land (₹279 cr)
history.impact: ₹60 cr deconsolidation gain; fewer, larger plants

history.event: Board approves merger of Krebs Biochemicals into Ipca (appointed date 1-Apr-2026)
history.impact: Tiny dilution (promoters 44.72% → 44.66%); secures a fermentation API used in Ipca's largest brand

notes: Exceptional items: FY24 −₹107.75 cr (EU fine provision at Unichem, deal costs, Krebs impairment, Optimus share gain), FY25 −₹205.05 cr (Krebs impairment ₹118.90 cr, Unichem land impairment ₹86.15 cr), FY26 −₹86.43 cr (EU interest, labour codes, land gain). Screener records them inside other income.
FY26 other income includes a one-off ₹60.04 cr gain on deconsolidating Bayshore and ₹27.38 cr of unrealised mutual-fund gains.
Forex: the company books exchange gains in other expenses (₹31.7 cr gain in Q1FY27); its reported EBITDA (22.88%) excludes it, Screener's (24.0%) includes it.
Minorities: 47.33% of Unichem and 41.12% of Trophic Wellness; ₹42.66 cr in FY26, ~₹21 cr in Q1FY27.
Working capital is heavy: inventory ~350 days of material cost (Screener), net working capital ~144 days (PL); Ipca keeps large API and raw-material stocks.
